purpose: Check whether the existing roughly four-month primer leaves initialization dependence in seasonal soil, vapor and rainfall feedbacks. Numerical equilibration experiment, not parameter optimization or a physics/atlas adoption gate.
control: Only extra complete spin-up years change. Preserve all physical parameters, planet properties, forcing fields, seasonal steps and strict per-step numerical criteria. The default0 run must reproduce archived T/P arrays exactly at their stored precision before any longer warm-up runs. Actual Earth case hashes must match the archived controls.
periodicity: For each pair of consecutive full years, compare all matching seasonal steps. Record maximum absolute changes over the domain interior and mapped land, plus mapped-land mean absolute changes. Fixed repeatability limits: temperature0.05C; rain0.01mm/day; column vapor0.05mm; soil water0.1mm; recycled-rain memory0.01mm/day; snow water0.1mm. These are numerical criteria, not fitted climate targets or real interannual variability.
interpretation: The three-extra-year case is the designated equilibrium candidate, never the lowest-error member of a search. One extra year is a sensitivity comparison. Report monthly T/P differences and observed Earth skill even if longer spin-up worsens skill. Require every per-step numerical solve; diagnose annual repeatability without suppressing nonperiodic results. No adaptive extra years or relaxed limits after seeing results.
publication: Default remains0. No new Earth physics or world climate is adopted by this pilot. Preserve existing atlas data and all earlier failed campaigns. A matched-layout initialization-sensitivity diagnostic may be added to the current r38 Earth atlas only if the unchanged baseline and source identities are verified; label its single-layout and screening-resolution scope. Any future default/profile adoption requires full matched Earth and world checks.
